```text
# Custom aliases cable channel for television (tv)
# Lists all runtime shell aliases and functions.
#
# Data source: ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt (generated by 12_television.zsh on
# shell startup). This avoids spawning `zsh -ic` which causes tty conflicts.
#
# Usage:
#   tv aliases                             (from shell)
#   Alt+A                                  (ZLE widget)
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Execute selected alias/function
#   Ctrl+Y     Copy alias/function name to clipboard
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Preview shows full definition via `type`.

[metadata]
name = "aliases"
description = "Shell aliases & functions: fuzzy search all shortcuts"

[source]
command = "cat ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt 2>/dev/null || echo 'Cache not found. Open a new shell to generate it.'"

[preview]
command = """
name='{split: :0}'
kind='{split: :1}'
if [ "$kind" = "alias" ]; then
  grep "^$name[[:space:]]" ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt 2>/dev/null
else
  zsh --no-rcs -c "autoload -Uz $name 2>/dev/null; whence -f $name 2>/dev/null" 2>/dev/null || echo "$name (function)"
fi
"""

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:exec"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy"

[actions.exec]
description = "Execute selected alias/function"
command = "{split: :0}"
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy]
description = "Copy name to clipboard"
command = """
if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | pbcopy
elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | wl-copy
elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | xclip -selection clipboard
fi
"""
mode = "fork"
----
# Cable channel: browse all tv channels with descriptions
#
# Usage:
#   tv channels
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Open selected channel in tv
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Preview shows the full TOML configuration for the selected channel.

[metadata]
name = "channels"
description = "Browse all available tv channels with descriptions"

[source]
command = """awk 'FILENAME!=prev{section=""; prev=FILENAME} /^\\[/{section=$0} section=="[metadata]" && /^name =/{name=$0; gsub(/.*= *"|"$/,"",name)} section=="[metadata]" && /^description =/{desc=$0; gsub(/.*= *"|"$/,"",desc); printf "%-30s │ %s\\n", name, desc}' ~/.config/television/cable/*.toml"""

[preview]
command = "bat -n --color=always ~/.config/television/cable/'{split: :0}'.toml 2>/dev/null || cat ~/.config/television/cable/'{split: :0}'.toml"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:open"

[actions.open]
description = "Open selected channel in tv"
command = "tv '{split: :0}'"
mode = "execute"
----
# Custom tools cable channel for television (tv)
# Parses ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md at runtime — single source of truth.
#
# Usage:
#   tv tools                               (from shell)
#   prefix + U in tmux                     (popup)
#   Alt+T in zsh                           (opens fzf ZLE variant instead)
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Execute selected tool immediately
#   Ctrl+T     Show tldrf page (multi-language fallback) in terminal
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Preview shows tldr page (zh_TW → zh → en fallback) or --help output.

[metadata]
name = "tools"
description = "CLI tools quick-launch: select a tool to execute it"
requirements = ["awk"]

[source]
command = """
awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
  inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
  desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/,"",desc)
  printf "%-22s  %s\\n", inv, desc
}' ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md
"""

[preview]
command = """
tool=$(printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | sed 's/ *$//')
if command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tldr -L zh_TW -L zh -L en "$tool" 2>/dev/null || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
else
  "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
fi
"""

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:exec"
ctrl-t = "actions:tldrf"

[actions.exec]
description = "Execute selected tool"
command = "{split: :0}"
mode = "execute"

[actions.tldrf]
description = "Show tldr page (multi-language fallback)"
command = "zsh -ic 'tldrf {split: :0}'"
mode = "execute"
----
# Custom keybindings cable channel for television (tv)
# Reads the same data source as the `keys-picker` ZLE widget (Alt+/) and
# the `bindings` shell function: ~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md
#
# Format contract (enforced by the picker too): every row is
#   | `<KEY>` | `<widget>` | <description> |
# parsed by awk -F'|' on lines that start with `| \``.
#
# Usage:
#   tv keybindings                          (CLI)
#   bindings                                (shell function fallback)
#   Alt+/                                   (ZLE widget — the canonical entry)
#
# Keybindings inside the picker:
#   Enter      Paste "# <key> → <widget>: <desc>" comment
#   Ctrl+Y     Copy the key combo to clipboard
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel (live `bindkey` lookup + source grep)

[metadata]
name = "keybindings"
description = "Zsh keybindings cheatsheet: search built-in / plugin / custom widgets"

[source]
command = """
awk -F'|' '
    /^[[:space:]]*\\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
        key=$2; widget=$3; desc=$4
        for (i in arr) delete arr[i]
        n = split("key widget desc", arr, " ")
        for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
            v = (arr[i] == "key") ? key : (arr[i] == "widget") ? widget : desc
            gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
            gsub(/^`|`$/, "", v)
            if (arr[i] == "key")    key = v
            if (arr[i] == "widget") widget = v
            if (arr[i] == "desc")   desc = v
        }
        if (key == "Key" || key ~ /^-+$/) next
        if (key == "<KEY>") next
        printf "%-16s  %-32s  %s\\n", key, widget, desc
    }
' ~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md
"""

[preview]
command = """
key=$(printf '%s' '{}' | awk '{print $1}')
widget=$(printf '%s' '{}' | awk '{print $2}')
echo "Key:    $key"
echo "Widget: $widget"
echo
echo '── Live bindkey lookup (emacs keymap) ──'
case "$key" in
  Ctrl+*)
    ksym=$(printf '^%s' "${key#Ctrl+}")
    bindkey -M emacs "$ksym" 2>/dev/null || echo '(not bound)'
    ;;
  Alt+*)
    rest=${key#Alt+}
    rest=$(printf '%s' "$rest" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
# Custom Aliases & Shell Functions

Quick reference for custom aliases and shell functions defined in this dotfiles repo. Available in zsh, bash, or both — the source file path tells you which:

- `dot_config/shell/*.sh` — POSIX layer, sourced by **both** `~/.zshrc` and `~/.bashrc`.
- `dot_config/zsh/*.zsh` (or `tools/*.zsh`) — **zsh-only**.
- `dot_config/bash/*.bash` — **bash-only**.

> **Maintenance rule** (mirrored in `CLAUDE.md`): whenever you add, modify, or remove a custom alias or shell function in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/`, update this table — include the type (`alias` or `function`), source file (relative to repo root), and a one-line description. Place new helpers in the right tier per the [CLAUDE.md three-tier rule](../../CLAUDE.md#custom-aliases--shell-functions--docsshellsaliasesmd).
```

```text
The ansible roles section is split into thematic subsections because

### 1. Bootstrap scripts (pre-chezmoi)
### 5. uv (Python CLI tools)

**Config**: `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` (+
`llm_tools/defaults/main.yml` for `litellm`). Role-level dispatch:
`dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`.

Inspects whether `uv` is below `min_uv_version` (`0.8.5`) and dispatches
the upgrade through the right channel — `brew upgrade uv` for Homebrew
installs, `uv self update` for the curl-installer. Mirror logic in
`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()`. See
[`docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`](uv-bootstrap.md) and
[`pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md).

Two install-completeness guards repair an existing tool without turning the role into an
upgrade loop: `extra_binaries` checks entry-point shims in `~/.local/bin`, while
`required_distributions` (paired with `env_name`) checks packages inside the uv tool venv.
A missing declaration triggers one `uv tool install --force`; a complete environment remains
unchanged. `yt-dlp[default]` uses the latter to ensure its matched `yt-dlp-ejs` solver is
present on hosts that previously installed bare `yt-dlp`.
```

```text
# 12_television.zsh - Television (tv) shell integration
#
# Tab completion via ~/.zfunc/_tv (regenerated on version change).
# We do NOT use `tv init zsh` because it binds Ctrl+T and Ctrl+R,
# which conflict with fzf's shell integration.
#
# Instead, tv channels are bound to Alt keys:
#   Alt+R  tv shell history     (tv-style history search)
#   Alt+P  tv files             (tv-style file/path picker)
#   Alt+G  tv git-log           (git log browser)
#   Alt+E  tv env               (environment variables)
#   Alt+A  tv aliases           (all aliases & functions)
#   Alt+I  tv git-ops           (insert git command from VSCode/GitLens menu)
#
# fzf keeps Ctrl+T / Ctrl+R / Alt+C (muscle memory).
# tv gets Alt namespace for advanced pickers.
#
# Aliases cache: ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt is generated on shell startup
# so that `tv aliases` channel can read it without spawning `zsh -ic`
# (which causes tty suspend issues).
#
# See: https://github.com/alexpasmantier/television

command -v tv &>/dev/null || return 0

# --- Tab completion (written to ~/.zfunc/, picked up by compinit) ---
if [[ -d ~/.zfunc ]]; then
  local _tv_ver="$(tv --version 2>/dev/null)"
  if [[ ! -f ~/.zfunc/_tv ]] || ! grep -q "${_tv_ver}" ~/.zfunc/_tv 2>/dev/null; then
    tv completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tv 2>/dev/null
  fi
fi

# --- Generate aliases cache for tv aliases channel ---
{
  mkdir -p ~/.cache/tv
  {
    alias | while IFS="=" read -r name rest; do
      printf "%-22s  alias   %s\n" "$name" "$rest"
    done
    typeset -f + | while read -r name; do
      printf "%-22s  func\n" "$name"
    done
  } | sort > ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt
} &>/dev/null &!

# --- Custom ZLE widgets for tv channels ---

_tv_channel_widget() {
  emulate -L zsh
  zle -I
  local output
  output=$(tv "$1" --no-status-bar --inline < /dev/tty)
  zle reset-prompt
  if [[ -n $output ]]; then
    LBUFFER+="$output"
  fi
}

_tv_history() {
  emulate -L zsh
  zle -I
  local output current_prompt
  current_prompt=$LBUFFER
  output=$(history -n -1 0 | tv --no-status-bar --input "$current_prompt" --inline < /dev/tty)
  zle reset-prompt
  if [[ -n $output ]]; then
    RBUFFER=""
    LBUFFER="$output"
  fi
}

_tv_files()   { _tv_channel_widget "files"; }
_tv_gitlog()  { _tv_channel_widget "git-log"; }
_tv_env()     { _tv_channel_widget "env"; }
_tv_aliases() { _tv_channel_widget "aliases"; }
_tv_gitops()  { _tv_channel_widget "git-ops"; }

zle -N tv-history  _tv_history
zle -N tv-files    _tv_files
zle -N tv-gitlog   _tv_gitlog
zle -N tv-env      _tv_env
zle -N tv-aliases  _tv_aliases
zle -N tv-gitops   _tv_gitops

# --- Keybindings (Alt namespace) ---
# Note: Alt+F is reserved for forward-word (emacs mode default).
bindkey '\er' tv-history   # Alt+R
bindkey '\ep' tv-files     # Alt+P (path/pick)
bindkey '\eg' tv-gitlog    # Alt+G
bindkey '\ee' tv-env       # Alt+E
bindkey '\ea' tv-aliases   # Alt+A
bindkey '\ei' tv-gitops    # Alt+I (insert git op)
```

```text
# Python CLI tools installed via uv tool install
# Each tool has:
#   - name: package name (can include extras like [cli])
#   - binary: executable name to check for idempotency
#   - with: (optional) additional dependency to install with --with
#   - with_executables_from: (optional) list of packages to install AND
#     expose their entry points in ~/.local/bin (e.g. jupyter-core to get
#     the `jupyter` meta-CLI; `notebook` to get `jupyter-notebook`)
#     NOTE: requires uv >= 0.8.5 (--with-executables-from added in that release)
#     For the meta-CLI dispatch model + the 8 jupyter binaries this exposes,
#     see docs/tools/notebooks.md "The `jupyter` meta-CLI vs standalone binaries".
#     For the auto-upgrade dispatch when uv is too old, see docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md.
#   - required_distributions: (optional) Python distributions that must exist
#     inside the installed tool environment, even when the primary binary is
#     already present. Requires env_name so the role can locate the uv venv.
#     Missing distributions trigger an idempotent `uv tool install --force`.
#   - env_name: (required with required_distributions) uv tool environment dir.
#   - extra_binaries: (optional) list of additional binary names that must
#     also exist in ~/.local/bin for the install to be considered complete.
#     Use this whenever `with_executables_from` is set, so adding a new
#     entry-point package later triggers a `--force` reinstall on machines
#     that already have `binary` present from a prior apply. Without this,
#     ansible's `creates:` guard short-circuits the install command and the
#     new exec shims are never written. See
#     pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md.
#   - python: (optional) pin Python version (e.g. "3.11" for thefuck)
#   - needs_modern_gcc: (optional, default false) tool transitively pulls
#     numpy 2.x / pandas 3.x / pyarrow which require GCC ≥ 9.3 to compile
#     from source. Skipped on systems where GCC < 9 (e.g. CentOS 7's
#     gcc 4.8.5). uv falls back to source build because numpy 2.x
#     dropped manylinux_2_17 wheels — see
#     pitfalls/centos7-numpy-pandas-source-build.md.

python_uv_tools:
  - name: thefuck
    binary: thefuck
    python: "3.11"  # Python 3.13 removed distutils which thefuck still uses
  - name: apprise
    binary: apprise
  - name: sqlit-tui[ssh]
    binary: sqlit
    needs_modern_gcc: true  # textual-fastdatatable -> pandas -> numpy 2.x
    with:
      - psycopg2-binary
      - pymysql
      - mssql-python
      - pyodbc
      - duckdb
  - name: python-dotenv[cli]
```

```text
1:# television (tv) Quick Reference
9:## Basic Usage
22:## Community Channels
40:## Custom Channels
42:### `tools` channel
53:For pasting an invocation to the shell buffer (with trailing space for tools that need arguments), use the fzf ZLE widget instead: **Alt+T** in any zsh session.
57:### `agent-wakeup` channel
61:`prefix + Alt+A`.
64:any queued pueue wakeup task. `Alt+C` schedules `continue` at the detected
65:reset time plus a small buffer, `Alt+T` prompts for a custom time/delay,
66:`Alt+N` smart-sends immediately (`Enter` for Claude's `/rate-limit-options`
67:screen, otherwise `continue` + Enter), and `Alt+X` cancels queued wakeups.
75:### `tailnet` channel
93:**Keybindings** (`Alt+` namespace avoids tmux/TV conflicts):
98:| `Alt+W` | `tsnet ssh-config` — write a managed `~/.ssh/config.d` block |
99:| `Alt+Z` | `tsnet --host <device> doctor` — tailnet-HTTPS / serve readiness |
100:| `Alt+T` | BatchMode SSH probe — does passwordless login actually work? |
101:| `Alt+P` | `tailscale ping` — direct path vs DERP-relayed |
102:| `Alt+Y` | Copy the MagicDNS FQDN (OSC 52 over SSH) |
104:`Alt+W` and `Alt+Z` were the only two `Alt` letters unused across every channel in
105:this repo, and are spent here on the two verbs that exist nowhere else. `Alt+T`
106:and `Alt+Y` keep their established meanings on purpose — muscle memory across
115:### `lan-devices` channel
137:**Keybindings** (`Alt+` namespace avoids tmux/TV conflicts):
142:| `Alt+R` | Rescan ports on selected host + reload |
143:| `Alt+F` | Rescan full subnet (discover + ports) + reload |
144:| `Alt+D` | Re-discover only (no port scan) + reload |
145:| `Alt+S` | SSH to selected host |
146:| `Alt+H` | Open `http://<ip>` in the system browser |
147:| `Alt+C` | Clear scan cache + reload |
164:### `logs` channel
174:3. **Linux only** — `journalctl --output=short-iso -n 2000` for systemd journal recent lines. Templated out on macOS because journalctl output lines are not file paths and the preview/Enter/Alt+T actions can't act on them (a dedicated `tv journalctl` channel would be the follow-up).
186:| `Alt+T` | Follow with `tspin --follow` (or `tail -F \| tspin --print` on older tailspin) |
187:| `Alt+E` | Open in `$EDITOR` |
194:### `services` channel
206:5. **Installed on-disk** — every unit file / `.plist` on disk, with enablement badges (`✓ Enabled` / `○ Disabled` / `— Static` / `⊘ Masked` on Linux; `● Loaded` / `○ On-disk` on macOS). This is the "configured but not enabled" discovery view — land on a `○ Disabled` row, hit `Alt+L`, done.
218:| `Alt+R` | Restart (auto-sudo when scope=system) |
219:| `Alt+S` | Stop (`systemctl stop` / `launchctl bootout`) |
220:| `Alt+T` | Start (`systemctl start` / `launchctl kickstart` with bootstrap-by-search fallback) |
221:| `Alt+U` | Reload (`reload-or-restart` / `launchctl kickstart`) |
222:| `Alt+D` | Show full status in pager |
223:| `Alt+E` | Edit unit file / plist in `$EDITOR` |
224:| `Alt+L` | Toggle enable-on-boot |
235:### `mac-procs` channel (macOS-only)
261:### `ansible` channel
280:**Keybindings** (`Alt+` namespace avoids tmux/TV conflicts):
285:| `Alt+C` | Syntax check (`--syntax-check`) |
286:| `Alt+D` | Dry run (`--check`) |
287:| `Alt+T` | Run OS-default playbook filtered by the selected tag/role |
288:| `Alt+E` | Edit file in `$EDITOR` (playbook YAML or role's `tasks/main.yml`) |
289:| `Alt+V` | Open role directory in `yazi` (roles source only) |
290:| `Ctrl+Y` / `Alt+Y` | Copy full `ansible-playbook ...` command to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH) |
296:### `git-ops` channel
302:Open with `tv git-ops` (standalone) or press `Alt+I` in zsh to paste the selected command straight into the shell prompt.
306:| `Enter` | Print selected command to stdout — captured by the `Alt+I` ZLE widget and inserted into `LBUFFER` |
308:| `Alt+E` | Confirm-prompt then `eval` the command (y/N); aborts by default on anything else |
312:> `Alt+E` (not `Ctrl+E`) is used for execute so that TV's global `Ctrl+E = go_to_input_end` muscle memory is preserved inside the picker.
314:Destructive rows (`commit --amend`, `reset --hard`, `push --force`, `branch -D`, `clean -fd`, `stash drop/clear`, `tag -d` on remote, rebase, etc.) are prefixed with `⚠` in the display line and trigger a red warning banner under `Alt+E`.
330:Columns are `Menu | Command | Alias | Description | Notes`. Leave the alias column blank (`| |`) if there's no oh-my-zsh alias; prefix with `*` if you're adding a custom function that lives in `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh`. See `docs/shells/aliases.md` for the full OMZ alias reference.
336:### `github-repos` / `gitlab-repos` channels
```

```text
config.toml.tmpl
{{- $noRoot := false }}{{ if hasKey . "noRoot" }}{{ $noRoot = .noRoot }}{{ end -}}
{{- /* installExtraRuntimes gates rust/bun/ruby (~1.8GB). Default TRUE when the
       key is absent so machines initialized before this prompt existed keep
       their runtimes until they re-init and answer explicitly. */ -}}
{{- $extraRuntimes := true }}{{ if hasKey . "installExtraRuntimes" }}{{ $extraRuntimes = .installExtraRuntimes }}{{ end -}}
{{- /* installDotnetTools gates the .NET SDK. Default FALSE when absent — this
       is the contract-bug fix: the prompt (default false) always promised to
       gate the SDK, but the SDK used to land unconditionally (~650MB even
       after answering No). See backlog/mise-runtime-gating.md. */ -}}
{{- $dotnet := false }}{{ if hasKey . "installDotnetTools" }}{{ $dotnet = .installDotnetTools }}{{ end -}}
{{- /* Detect CentOS/RHEL 7 — glibc 2.17 + libstdc++ from gcc 4.8.5. Modern
       Node (18+) / Bun musl / .NET 6+ binaries refuse to load against this
       baseline, and mise's rustup channel is gated on a TUNA mirror that
       garbage-collects old versions. We skip those tools on this host class
       and document the manual fallbacks (NodeSource RPM, direct rustup,

  {{- $verID := "" -}}

  {{- if and (or (eq $id "centos") (eq $id "rhel") (eq $id "scientific") (contains "rhel" $idLike)) (eq $verID "7") -}}
    {{- $oldEL = true -}}

{{- end -}}

# https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration.html

[settings]
# Use precompiled ruby binaries instead of compiling from source.
# ruby-build needs libffi-dev + a working C toolchain; precompiled avoids all that.
ruby.compile = false
{{ if and $dotnet (not $oldEL) -}}
# Keep SDKs in their version directories, including installs made before mise's
# shared dotnet-root default. mise exports DOTNET_ROOT for global tool apphosts.
# See pitfalls/azure-cost-you-must-install-dotnet.md.
dotnet.isolated = true
{{ end -}}

[env]
# mise's Go backend force-sets GOBIN=<mise install>/bin with NO off-switch
# (settings expose go_set_gopath / go_set_goroot but NOT go_set_gobin) and
# re-asserts it on every `cd` via hook-env, clobbering any shell export. So the
# ONLY reliable way to send `go install` into the blessed ~/.local/bin (instead
# of the version-pinned toolchain dir, which is wiped on every `go` upgrade) is
```

```text
1:#!/usr/bin/env bash
4:usage() {
6:        "Usage:" \
46:# Reach for OSC 52 before any local wl-copy/xclip/xsel? True when a local
47:# display-server tool would write to the wrong machine or a stale display:
48:#
49:#   - SSH: the clipboard we want is on the far end of the TTY, not this host.
50:#   - herdr: the pane environment is frozen at herdr-server start, so
51:#     $WAYLAND_DISPLAY / $SSH_CONNECTION there describe whoever launched the
52:#     daemon, not the client attached now. The pane's TTY, however, always
53:#     proxies to the real client (local or remote), so OSC 52 is correct
54:#     either way. tmux refreshes these vars via update-environment; herdr
55:#     doesn't. Same reasoning for $ZELLIJ.
56:#
57:# Overridden by X_CLIPBOARD (see clipboard_forced). Mirrors the Neovim gate in
58:# dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua.
-----
dev () {
	case "${1:-}" in
		(__complete|__completeNoDesc|--help|-h|--version|--skill|completion|config|doctor|retire|prepare|artifact|git|edit|gitignore|ignore|help|list|ls|park|skill|shell-init|cache|stats|status|sweep|adopt|bootstrap) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev "$@" || return $?
			return 0 ;;
	esac
	local __dev_cd_file __dev_action_file __dev_dir __dev_status
	local __dev_action __dev_task __dev_delete __dev_unknown
	if ! __dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" 
	then
		__dev_cd_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-cd.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"  || {
			printf 'dev: cannot create the shell directory side channel\n' >&2
			return 1
		}
	fi
	if ! __dev_action_file="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/dev-action.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" 
	then
		__dev_action_file="$(mktemp "/tmp/dev-action.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)"  || {
			rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" || :
			printf 'dev: cannot create the shell action side channel\n' >&2
			return 1
		}
	fi
	__dev_status=0 
	DEV_SHELL_CD_FD=3 DEV_SHELL_ACTION_FD=4 command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev "$@" 3> "$__dev_cd_file" 4> "$__dev_action_file" || __dev_status=$? 
	if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_cd_file" ]
	then
		if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_dir < "$__dev_cd_file"
		then
			if [ -n "$__dev_dir" ]
			then
				builtin cd -- "$__dev_dir" || __dev_status=$? 
			fi
		else
			__dev_status=1 
		fi
	fi
	if [ $__dev_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$__dev_action_file" ]
	then
		exec 4< "$__dev_action_file"
		if IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_action <&4 && IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_task <&4 && IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_delete <&4 && IFS= read -r -d '' __dev_unknown <&4 && {
				[ "$__dev_action" = retire ] || [ "$__dev_action" = retire-recursive ]
			}
		then
			if [ "$__dev_action" = retire-recursive ]
			then
				case "$__dev_delete:$__dev_unknown" in
					(false:false) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --recursive -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(true:false) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --recursive --delete-branch -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(false:true) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --recursive --close-unknown -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(true:true) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --recursive --delete-branch --close-unknown -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(*) __dev_status=1  ;;
				esac
			else
				case "$__dev_delete:$__dev_unknown" in
					(false:false) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(true:false) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --delete-branch -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(false:true) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --close-unknown -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(true:true) command /opt/homebrew/bin/dev retire --delete-branch --close-unknown -- "$__dev_task" || __dev_status=$?  ;;
					(*) __dev_status=1  ;;
				esac
			fi
		else
			__dev_status=1 
		fi
		exec 4<&-
	fi
	rm -f -- "$__dev_cd_file" "$__dev_action_file" || :
	return $__dev_status
}
```

```text
# Custom tools cable channel for television (tv)
# Parses ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md at runtime — single source of truth.
#
# Usage:
#   tv tools                               (from shell)
#   prefix + U in tmux                     (popup)
#   Alt+T in zsh                           (opens fzf ZLE variant instead)
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Execute selected tool immediately
#   Ctrl+T     Show tldrf page (multi-language fallback) in terminal
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Preview shows tldr page (zh_TW → zh → en fallback) or --help output.

[metadata]
name = "tools"
description = "CLI tools quick-launch: select a tool to execute it"
requirements = ["awk"]

[source]
command = """
awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
  inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
  desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/,"",desc)
  printf "%-22s  %s\\n", inv, desc
}' ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md
"""

[preview]
command = """
tool=$(printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | sed 's/ *$//')
if command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tldr -L zh_TW -L zh -L en "$tool" 2>/dev/null || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
else
  "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
fi
"""

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:exec"
ctrl-t = "actions:tldrf"

[actions.exec]
description = "Execute selected tool"
command = "{split: :0}"
mode = "execute"

[actions.tldrf]
description = "Show tldr page (multi-language fallback)"
command = "zsh -ic 'tldrf {split: :0}'"
mode = "execute"

### 11. curl-installer (self-managed CLIs)

Tools that ship via vendor `install.sh` instead of any package manager.
Mostly the AI coding agents (each vendor maintains their own installer
+ self-update subcommand). All landing paths are user-writable so
in-binary self-update works without sudo.

**Inventory**:

| Tool | Install URL | Lands at | Source role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Homebrew | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh` | `/usr/local/bin/brew` (macOS) / `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/` (Linux) | bootstrap |
| uv | `https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh` | `~/.local/bin/uv` (or `~/.cargo/bin/uv`) | bootstrap |
| mise | `https://mise.run` | `~/.local/bin/mise` | bootstrap |
| just | `https://just.systems/install.sh` | `/usr/local/bin/just` or `~/.local/bin/just` | `base` |
| starship | `https://starship.rs/install.sh` | `/usr/local/bin/starship` or `~/.local/bin/starship` | `starship` |
| atuin | `https://setup.atuin.sh` | `~/.atuin/bin/atuin` | `atuin` |
| docker | `https://get.docker.com` | system docker (rootless variant) | `docker` (Linux) |
| zoxide | (vendor installer) | `~/.local/bin/zoxide` | `devtools` (Linux fallback) |
| direnv | (vendor installer) | `~/.local/bin/direnv` | `devtools` (Linux fallback) |
| **Claude Code** | `https://claude.ai/install.sh` | `~/.claude/local/bin/claude` | `coding_agents` (Linux) |
| **OpenCode** | `https://opencode.ai/install` (+ `--no-modify-path`) | `~/.opencode/bin/opencode` | `coding_agents` (macOS + Linux) |
```

There is one tv channel for aliases and shell functions. It reads the aliases and functions defined in the running shell, not `docs/shells/aliases.md`. The two share no code.

## 1. The aliases channel

**File:** `/Users/zhouhanru/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/aliases.toml` (the only one; nothing else in `dot_dotfiles/bin/` or `scripts/` produces this data)

**Where the data comes from:** at each zsh startup, `/Users/zhouhanru/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/zsh/tools/12_television.zsh` asks the shell for its aliases and functions and writes them to a cache file in the background:
```zsh
{ alias | while IFS="=" read -r name rest; do printf "%-22s  alias   %s\n" "$name" "$rest"; done
  typeset -f + | while read -r name; do printf "%-22s  func\n" "$name"; done
} | sort > ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt   # backgrounded with &!
```
- The channel just runs `cat ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt`, with a "Cache not found. Open a new shell" fallback.
- The file comment says it avoids `zsh -ic` because that "causes tty conflicts".
- Only zsh writes the cache, so bash-only aliases never show up.
- Nothing is filtered out. The current cache has 2696 lines, including internal ones like `__arguments` and `_`, plus oh-my-zsh and plugin functions.

**Preview:** a shell snippet, not bat. It uses `{split: :0}` (the name) and `{split: :1}` (the kind), splitting on spaces rather than tabs.
- For an alias, it greps the cache line.
- For a function, it runs `zsh --no-rcs -c "autoload -Uz $name; whence -f $name"`. Functions defined in rc files aren't loaded in that shell, so the preview mostly falls back to printing `name (function)`. The header comment says "Preview shows full definition via `type`", but the code doesn't use `type`.

**Keys:**
- `enter` runs `actions:exec`: `command = "{split: :0}"`, `mode = "execute"`.
- `ctrl-y` runs `actions:copy`: tries pbcopy, then wl-copy, then xclip, with `mode = "fork"`.
- The channel has no Alt+ actions.

**How to open it:** `tv aliases`, or **Alt+A** in zsh. Alt+A is the `tv-aliases` widget (`bindkey '\ea'`), which calls `_tv_channel_widget "aliases"` and adds the output to `LBUFFER` (the text before the cursor).

## 2. How `docs/shells/aliases.md` relates
- The channel doesn't use it at all. It's a hand-maintained table: `| Command | Type | Source File | Description |`, with sections like Editor and Git.
- `CLAUDE.md` line 17 requires a row in it whenever an alias or function in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` changes.
- It isn't deployed to `~/.config/docs/`. Only these three are:
  - `dot_config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`
  - `dot_config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md`
  - `dot_config/docs/tools/git-ops.md`
- Those three are markdown "data source" files for the `keybindings`, `tools` and `git-ops` channels. Each is parsed at runtime with `awk -F'|'` on rows starting with `` | ` ``.
- So if you want a curated aliases channel with descriptions, those three channels are the existing pattern to copy.

## 3. All cable files (`dot_config/television/cable/`)
One-line purposes are taken from each file's `description`.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| agent-panes.toml | Live coding-agent panes across tmux; jump to a running session |
| agent-sessions.toml | Content-searchable OpenCode / Claude / Codex / Cursor sessions |
| agent-wakeup.toml | Agent quota wait/reset dashboard and scheduled `continue` tasks |
| aliases.toml | Shell aliases and functions (runtime cache) |
| ansible.toml | Ansible playbooks, roles and tags: syntax-check, run, copy command |
| appsrc-size.toml | Installed apps by disk footprint |
| appsrc.toml | Installed apps and CLIs, and how each was installed |
| audit-events.toml | auditd events (aureport / ausearch) |
| azure.toml | Azure resources: restart / deallocate / rotate-ip, portal |
| channels.toml | Browse all tv channels (awk over `[metadata]` name/description) |
| clash-api.toml | Live Clash/mihomo controller |
| clash.toml | Clash/mihomo config: proxies, rules, latency |
| disk.toml.tmpl | Filesystem usage triage |
| firewall.toml.tmpl | Firewall rules and sockets (multi-backend) |
| fleet-hosts.toml | Fleet hosts from `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml` |
| git-ops.toml | VSCode / GitLens git operations (parses `docs/tools/git-ops.md`) |
| github-repos.toml / gitlab-repos.toml | Fuzzy-find your repos: README preview, open, clone |
| herdr-agent-panes.toml | Live herdr panes |
| herdr-review.toml | herdr panes flagged for review (⭐) |
| herdr-sesh.toml | herdr workspace switcher plus zoxide |
| keybindings.toml | Zsh keybindings cheatsheet (parses `keybindings.md`) |
| kill-process.toml | Kill a process, with CPU/MEM stats |
| lan-devices.toml | LAN devices: IP, MAC, vendor, ports |
| linux-apps.toml.tmpl / mac-apps.toml.tmpl | GUI app quit / restart / activate |
| logs.toml.tmpl | Log files with tailspin/lnav preview |
| mac-procs.toml.tmpl | macOS processes sorted by memory |
| mlflow.toml | MLflow experiments, runs and models |
| ports.toml | Listening ports |
| pueue.toml | Pueue tasks |
| rclone-help.toml / rclone.toml | rclone command reference / remotes browser |
| scheduled-jobs.toml.tmpl | cron / systemd timers / at / launchd |
| services-health.toml.tmpl | Failed units, restart loops, OOM kills |
| services.toml.tmpl | systemd / launchd service control |
| sesh.toml.reference | Reference copy of the community sesh channel (not `.toml`, so not a live channel) |
| sessions.toml.tmpl | Login sessions |
| skills-walk.toml / skills.toml | Agent skills (filesystem walk / `npx skills`) |
| sms.toml | Huawei router SMS inbox |
| ssh-config.toml | SSH hosts, including grouped `config.d` |
| sudo-history.toml | sudo events |
| super-productivity.toml | Super Productivity tasks (read-only) |
| sysadmin.toml.tmpl | Launcher for all sysadmin / audit channels |
| tailnet.toml | Tailscale devices |
| tools.toml | CLI tools quick-launch (parses `cli-tools.md`) |
| users.toml.tmpl | Local user account inventory |
| wifi-scan.toml | Nearby Wi-Fi |
| yth.toml | YouTube watch history |

Helper scripts sit beside the cable directory in `dot_config/television/`, e.g. `executable_*-source.sh` and `executable_*-preview.sh`.

## 4. Conventions
- **Header comment block** in each file, listing Usage and Keybindings. Then `[metadata]` with `name` and `description` (the `channels` channel depends on these), optional `requirements`, then `[source]`, `[preview]`, `[keybindings]`, and `[actions.X]` with a `description`, a `command` and a `mode` of `execute` or `fork`.
- **Alt+ for channel actions.** Per `docs/tools/tv.md`: "`Alt+` namespace avoids tmux/TV conflicts", and tmux's prefix `Ctrl+b` never reaches tv. Letters are reused on purpose across channels: Alt+E edit, Alt+T follow/start, Alt+Y copy (OSC 52 over SSH), Alt+R restart/rescan. Paired TUI and channel CLIs (`mlf`, `yth`, `appsrc`) must use the same letters in the TUI and in tv (`CLAUDE.md` line 22). Older channels like aliases and tools still use `ctrl-y` / `ctrl-t`.
- **bat preview:** e.g. `channels.toml` uses `bat -n --color=always … || cat …`.
- **Field splitting:** tab-separated sources use `{split:\t:N}` (appsrc's TSV column order is a wire format). Simpler channels such as aliases and channels use `{split: :0}`.
- **`.toml.tmpl`:** used for OS-dependent channels (disk, firewall, logs, services, mac/linux-apps, and others), rendered by chezmoi templates.
- **zsh Alt bindings** in `12_television.zsh`: Alt+R history, Alt+P files, Alt+G git-log, Alt+E env, Alt+A aliases, Alt+I git-ops. It deliberately doesn't use `tv init zsh`, so fzf keeps Ctrl+T and Ctrl+R.

## 5. Docs and registration
- There's no registry: tv picks up any `*.toml` in `~/.config/television/cable/`, and `tv channels` lists them.
- Docs are in `/Users/zhouhanru/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/tv.md`, under a "Custom Channels" section with one `###` per channel. It covers tools, agent-wakeup, tailnet, lan-devices, logs, services, mac-procs, ansible, git-ops, github/gitlab-repos, pueue, azure, clash and sesh. **The aliases channel isn't documented there**; it's only mentioned in the header of `12_television.zsh`.
- There's also `docs/tools/tv-vs-fzf.md`.

## 6. Tests
There's no generic channel test and nothing for aliases. Channel-specific tests:
- `tests/unit/test_ssh_tv_source.py` loads `cable/ssh-config.toml`.
- `tests/unit/editorcfg.bats` line 149 greps `disk.toml.tmpl`.
- `tests/unit/tsnet_ssh_block.bats` checks that the ssh-config awk agrees with the other two SSH-config parsers.
- `lan_scan.bats` and `agent_wakeup.bats` test the helper scripts behind their channels.

````text
# Custom tools cable channel for television (tv)
# Parses ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md at runtime — single source of truth.
#
# Usage:
#   tv tools                               (from shell)
#   prefix + U in tmux                     (popup)
#   Alt+T in zsh                           (opens fzf ZLE variant instead)
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Execute selected tool immediately
#   Ctrl+T     Show tldrf page (multi-language fallback) in terminal
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# Preview shows tldr page (zh_TW → zh → en fallback) or --help output.

[metadata]
name = "tools"
description = "CLI tools quick-launch: select a tool to execute it"
requirements = ["awk"]

[source]
command = """
awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
  inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
  desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/,"",desc)
  printf "%-22s  %s\\n", inv, desc
}' ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md
"""

[preview]
command = """
tool=$(printf '%s' '{split: :0}' | sed 's/ *$//')
if command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tldr -L zh_TW -L zh -L en "$tool" 2>/dev/null || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
else
  "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50
fi
"""

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:exec"
ctrl-t = "actions:tldrf"

[actions.exec]
description = "Execute selected tool"
command = "{split: :0}"
mode = "execute"

[actions.tldrf]
description = "Show tldr page (multi-language fallback)"
command = "zsh -ic 'tldrf {split: :0}'"
mode = "execute"

# CLI Tools Reference

All tools installed by this dotfiles project. The **Invocation** column is what gets pasted to the shell buffer by the `tools-picker` (Alt+T) and TV channel (`tv tools`). Tools with a trailing space need an argument before running.

> **Source of truth for the interactive pickers**: both `tv tools` and the fzf ZLE widget (Alt+T) parse this file at runtime.

---

## File & Search

| Command | Invocation | Description | Notes |
|---------|------------|-------------|-------|
| `rg` | `rg ` | Fast regex search (ripgrep) | `-l` files only, `-i` case-insensitive, `-t` by filetype |
| `fd` | `fd ` | Fast file finder | `-t f` files, `-t d` dirs, `-e ext` by extension |
| `bat` | `bat ` | cat with syntax highlighting | `--plain`, `--paging=never`, `-l` language |
| `eza` | `eza ` | Modern ls with git status | aliases: `ls`, `la`, `ll`, `lt`, `llt` |
| `fzf` | `fzf` | Interactive fuzzy finder | `Ctrl+T` files, `Ctrl+R` history, `Alt+C` cd |
| `yazi` | `yazi` | TUI file manager (cd on exit) | alias `y` for cd-on-exit wrapper |
| `glow` | `glow ` | Render Markdown in terminal | `glow -p` paged |
| `duckdb` | `duckdb ` | In-process SQL analytics | `.open file.db` to open, `.tables` to list |
| `rclone` | `rclone ` | Sync files to/from cloud storage | `rclone sync src dst` |

## Git & Diff

| Command | Invocation | Description | Notes |
|---------|------------|-------------|-------|
| `lazygit` | `lazygit` | Git TUI | alias `lg` |

| `delta` | `delta ` | Diff pager with syntax highlight | configured as default git pager |
| `diffnav` | `diffnav` | TUI diff navigator | `diffnav <file>` or pipe from `git diff` |
| `git-graph` | `git-graph` | Visual branch graph | `git-graph --all` |
| `gitleaks` | `gitleaks ` | Secret scanner | `gitleaks detect`, `gitleaks protect` |
| `pre-commit` | `pre-commit ` | Git hook manager | `pre-commit run --all-files`, `pre-commit install` |

# appsrc channel — browse the full installed inventory + how each was installed.
#
# Thin channel: all detection lives in the `appsrc` CLI
# (dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_appsrc). This file just shells out:
#   appsrc scan --tsv                 (source — name<TAB>source<TAB>path<TAB>kind<TAB>package)
#   appsrc which --path '<path>'      (preview + Enter detail; --path is unambiguous)
# so the picker tracks the CLI automatically (no parallel logic to keep in sync).
#
# Full GUI+CLI inventory (~thousands) — fuzzy-type a source label (cask / manual
# / app-store / apt / snap …) or a name to narrow. For the biggest space
# consumers use `tv appsrc-size` instead.
#
# Non-templated: `appsrc` adapts to macOS/Linux internally, and the actions use
# portable clipboard / open fallbacks, so one file works on both.
#
# Usage:
#   tv appsrc
#
# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace — tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows Ctrl+):
#   Enter      Full detail (source + evidence: signer / bundle-id / origin URL)
#   Alt+S      Size report (bundle + associated storage: cache / data / containers)
#   Alt+T      tldr — quick usage (CLI tools)
#   Alt+M      man page (CLI tools)
#   Alt+C      Copy the app path to the clipboard
#   Alt+O      Reveal the app in Finder (macOS) / open it (Linux)
#   Alt+J      Detail as JSON (piped through a pager)
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel

[metadata]
name = "appsrc"
description = "Installed apps + CLIs — how each was installed (cask / App Store / direct / apt / snap / …)"
requirements = ["appsrc"]

[source]
command = "appsrc scan --tsv"
# name<TAB>source-label<TAB>path<TAB>kind<TAB>package
display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:1})  [{split:\\t:3}]"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[preview]
command = "appsrc which --path '{split:\\t:2}'"
header = "{split:\\t:0}  —  {split:\\t:1}"

[ui]
input_header = "Install source"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:detail"
alt-s = "actions:size"
alt-t = "actions:tldr"
alt-m = "actions:man"
alt-c = "actions:copy-path"
alt-o = "actions:reveal"
alt-j = "actions:json"

[actions.detail]
description = "Full source + evidence detail"
command = "appsrc which --path '{split:\\t:2}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

# `appsrc` — how was this app installed?

`appsrc` answers a question no single OS command does: **where did this app come
from — Homebrew cask, the Mac App Store, a direct-download dmg/pkg, apt, snap,
flatpak, an AppImage, a language package manager, or a manual drop-in?** It
combines several signals, ordered by specificity, and captures the evidence.

- Source: [`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_appsrc`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_appsrc) (single-file `uv run --script`, `rich`-only)
- Deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/appsrc` (on PATH); run from the repo via `just appsrc …`
- Picker twin: `tv appsrc` · Completions: `57_appsrc_completion.{zsh,bash}`

## Usage

```console
# Single lookup (live, no cache) — a shell command OR a GUI app name:
$ appsrc which docker
docker  (Homebrew cask)
  kind       cli
  path       /Applications/Docker.app/Contents/Resources/bin/docker
  package    docker-desktop
  note       CLI shim into Docker.app

$ appsrc which "Google Chrome"          # GUI app by name
$ appsrc firefox                        # bare word == `appsrc which firefox`
$ appsrc which --path /Applications/Foo.app   # classify a path directly

# Batch inventory (GUI apps + CLI tools), cached:
$ appsrc                 # == appsrc scan
$ appsrc scan --kind gui                # GUI apps only
$ appsrc scan --source cask             # filter by source id/label
$ appsrc scan --json | jq '.[] | select(.source=="manual")'
$ appsrc scan --tsv                     # name<TAB>source<TAB>path<TAB>kind<TAB>package
$ appsrc scan --refresh                 # ignore cache, recompute

# How much space does it cost (bundle + caches / data / containers)?
$ appsrc size docker                    # bundle + ~/Library/Containers/… + caches, totalled
$ appsrc size "Google Chrome" --json
$ appsrc scan --kind gui --size         # add a bundle-size column to the inventory

# Navigate the whole inventory interactively:
$ appsrc tui                            # sortable dashboard — `s` sorts by size, `/` filters
$ appsrc scan --sort size               # biggest first (implies --size)
```

`which` is always live and gathers full evidence (codesign signer, bundle id,
download-provenance URL). `scan` is cached (see below) and skips the slow
per-app forks for anything an authoritative inventory already claims.

## What it detects

| Source id | Label | Platform |
|---|---|---|
| `homebrew-cask` / `homebrew-formula` | Homebrew cask / formula | macOS |
| `mac-app-store` | Mac App Store | macOS |
| `direct-download-pkg` / `direct-download-dmg` | Direct download (pkg / dmg-web) | macOS |
| `apt` / `snap` / `flatpak` / `appimage` / `linuxbrew` | apt·dpkg / snap / flatpak / AppImage / Linuxbrew | Linux |
| `cargo` `npm` `pipx` `uv` `mise` `go` `gem` | language package managers | both |
| `macos-system` / `manual` / `unknown` | OS-bundled / hand-placed / unattributable | both |

Each record carries a `confidence` — `authoritative` (a manager explicitly owns
it) or `heuristic` (inferred from provenance/signing).

## How it decides (two passes)

**Pass A — forward inventory (authoritative).** Ask each manager once what it
owns and match in memory (no per-item forks): `brew list --cask` + a single
`brew info --cask --json=v2` to map `.app`→cask, `brew list --formula`,
`mas list`; on Linux `snap list` / `flatpak list` / `dpkg -S` / Linuxbrew prefix;
CLI tools by resolved-path prefix (`~/.cargo/bin`, `~/.local/share/uv`, …).

**Pass B — per-item heuristics.** For anything Pass A doesn't claim (and every
`which`), walk an ordered decision tree:

- **macOS `.app`**: Caskroom metadata → cask; `mas list` / App-Store receipt /
  Apple re-signing → App Store; `pkgutil --file-info` receipt → pkg;
  `mdls kMDItemWhereFroms` provenance URL → dmg/web; else manual. `codesign`
  Authority + `CFBundleIdentifier` are captured as tie-break evidence.
- **Linux command**: `realpath` → `/snap/` → snap; `/var/lib/flatpak` → flatpak;
  `.appimage` → AppImage; Linuxbrew prefix → linuxbrew; `dpkg -S`/`rpm -qf`
  owner → apt; `/usr/local` or `$HOME` unowned → manual.
````

| Path | Key | Shape |
|---|---|---|

| `llm_tools/defaults/main.yml` | `llm_tools_uv:` | Same shape as uv (`litellm[proxy]` / `litellm` / `python` / `with`), plus boolean flags |

| `ruby_gem_tools/defaults/main.yml` | `ruby_gem_tools:` | `name`, `binary` (try-cli → try, tmuxinator) |
| `dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml` | `dotnet_tools:` | `name`, `binary`, `smoke_args`; also `dotnet_version: "10"` |

## 4. Existing "tools list" CLIs
- **`tv tools`**, defined in `/Users/zhouhanru/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/tools.toml`. An awk command parses the markdown tables in `~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md` (source: `/Users/zhouhanru/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md`, 116 lines, 55 rows). The tables have the header `| Command | Invocation | Description | Notes |` and sit under category headings (File & Search, Git & Diff, …, AI / Coding Agents). The channel's preview shows a tldr page or `--help` output. It is also bound to tmux `prefix+U`, and the zsh `Alt+T` picker (`dot_config/zsh/tools/11_tools_picker.zsh`) reads the same file. This is a usage reference, not an install inventory, and it is separate from the tool-managers index.
- **`just info`** (`justfile` around line 397) prints "Installed tools:" with versions of chezmoi, ansible, nvim and git only.
- **`x`** (`dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x`) is a clipboard utility, not a tool lister.
- **`dev`** is an external binary at `/opt/homebrew/bin/dev` (a wrapper shell function calls it). Its `list`/`ls` subcommands cover repos and tasks, not installed tools.
- No other script in `dot_dotfiles/bin/` lists installed tools.

**Where should the tool list the channel reads be maintained? Right now there are two hand-written lists: the ~234-row Tool index in tool-managers.md, which records how each tool is installed but has no description or category, and cli-tools.md, 55 rows used by `tv tools`.**

Options:
- **Structured catalog file (Recommended)** - Add a machine-readable tool-catalog.toml as the single source of truth, holding name, binaries, category, description, install method per OS, ansible role/recipe and a doc link. Generate the tool-managers.md Tool index from it (drift check works like gen-prompts). Tests check that every tool in the role defaults lists (uv/npm/gem/dotnet/go) has an entry.
- **Parse tool-managers.md** - Add Category and Description columns to the existing Tool index table and parse it with awk, the same way `tv tools` parses its markdown. Less work up front, but the table format is loose (several tools per row, notes after the role), so parsing will be fragile.
- **Expand cli-tools.md** - Grow cli-tools.md from 55 to about 234 rows and add install-method and role columns. It then serves as both the usage reference and the install inventory. The table gets wide and gets mixed up with its launcher role.

- **Merge into tv tools** - Point `tv tools` at the new catalog and retire cli-tools.md. One fewer thing to maintain, but tools-picker (Alt+T) and the tmux prefix+U popup both depend on the current format and would need changes too.

````markdown
# Plan: `tv inventory` — a searchable catalog of tools this repo installs

## Context

The user keeps losing track of what the repo installs. Today that information is split across three places, and none of them answers "what is this, which role/recipe installs it, and is it on this host?":

- `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` § Tool index (A–Z): about 234 hand-written rows with columns `Tool | macOS | Linux | Role`. It has no category or description. The format is loose (several tools per row, `— notes` after the role), and nothing parses it or checks it for coverage.
- `dot_config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md`: 55 curated rows that drive `tv tools` and the Alt+T launcher. It is a launcher list, not an inventory.
- `tv appsrc`: a live scan of the OS (cask, apt, uv, …). It shows how something got onto the machine, but not whether this repo declared it or which role owns it.

The existing `tv aliases` channel, the precedent the user remembers, builds its list at runtime from `alias` / `typeset -f`. That works for aliases but not for tools: an install inventory needs data that has been *declared*.

**Outcome:** one structured catalog file becomes the single source of truth for tool metadata. A new `tv inventory` channel reads it and checks each tool's live status on this host, and the Tool index in tool-managers.md is generated from the catalog instead of being written by hand.

### How the user's two concerns are handled

1. **Duplication.** The catalog *replaces* the hand-written Tool index table, which becomes a generated marker region, so there is one fewer copy. It does **not** copy the role defaults lists: `python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml` and the others remain the install source of truth. The catalog only adds what they lack (category, description, docs link), and a test fails if a role list has a binary the catalog is missing. `cli-tools.md` stays as the curated launcher. Generating it from a `launcher = true` field is left to the backlog.
2. **Hosts that install only part of the set because of different init prompts.** Each role in the catalog records the prompt that gates it, e.g. `media_tools → installMediaTools`, mirroring the `{{ if $installMediaTools }}` gates in `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`. When the channel builds its list it reads `chezmoi data --format json` once and gives every row one of four statuses:
   - ✅ installed (`command -v` hits)
   - ❌ expected but missing (gate on, right OS, binary absent). This means the install is broken.
   - ⚪ not enabled on this host (prompt off). The detail view names the prompt key, so the user knows how to turn it on.
   - `–` not for this OS

   Fuzzy-typing `❌` or `⚪` then filters by status.

## Design

### 1. Catalog: `dot_config/docs/tools/tool-catalog.toml` (new, deployed next to `cli-tools.md`)

```toml
[roles.media_tools]
gate = "installMediaTools"        # prompt key; omit = always installed
[roles.devtools]                  # no gate

[[tool]]
name = "bat"
bin = ["bat"]                     # binaries to probe; default [name]
category = "File & Search"        # reuse cli-tools.md's category names
desc = "cat with syntax highlighting"
role = "devtools"                 # ansible role | "Brewfile.darwin" | "bootstrap" | "mise" | "chezmoi-external"
mac = "brew"
linux = "apt"                     # "n/a" means not for this OS
gate = ""                         # optional per-tool override (e.g. installPlaywrightCli inside a role)
docs = "docs/tools/bat.md"        # optional, repo-relative
```

The install and upgrade commands are *derived*, not stored:
- install: `just ansible-tags <role>`, or a Brewfile / mise note
- upgrade: `just upgrade-<manager>`, using a manager → category map that mirrors `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` `cat_*`

**Seeding:** write a one-off script to parse the existing 234-row Tool index into the TOML (names, mac/linux, role). Take descriptions and categories from `cli-tools.md` for its 55 overlapping tools, then have an agent draft the remaining roughly 180 `category`/`desc` values, with user review of the diff.

### 2. Helper: `dot_config/television/executable_tool-catalog.py`

- Uses a `uv run --script` PEP 723 header, the same pattern as `executable_mlflow-source.py`.
- Needs only the standard library (`tomllib`, requires-python >= 3.11).
- Subcommands:
  - `source`: TSV `name⇥status⇥category⇥role⇥method⇥desc`. The method is the current OS's `mac` or `linux` value. It calls `chezmoi data` once and probes with `shutil.which`; the whole list must stay under about 300 ms.
  - `preview NAME`: the full catalog entry, status with reason (including the gate key when ⚪), resolved path, a best-effort `--version` line with a short timeout, and the derived install/upgrade commands.
  - `index-md`: renders the Tool index markdown table. Used by `just gen-tool-index [--check]`, the same pattern as `just gen-prompts`, running the same file from the source tree.

### 3. Channel: `dot_config/television/cable/inventory.toml`

- Its header comment follows the convention in `appsrc.toml`.
- Source: `~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py source`.
- Display: `{split:\t:1} {split:\t:0}  [{split:\t:2}]  {split:\t:5}  ({split:\t:3})`.
- Preview: `tool-catalog.py preview '{split:\t:0}'`.
````

````text
# Plan: `tv inventory` — a searchable catalog of tools this repo installs

## Context

The user keeps losing track of what the repo installs. Today that information is split across three places, and none of them answers "what is this, which role/recipe installs it, and is it on this host?":

- `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` § Tool index (A–Z): about 234 hand-written rows with columns `Tool | macOS | Linux | Role`. It has no category or description. The format is loose (several tools per row, `— notes` after the role), and nothing parses it or checks it for coverage.
- `dot_config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md`: 55 curated rows that drive `tv tools` and the Alt+T launcher. It is a launcher list, not an inventory.
- `tv appsrc`: a live scan of the OS (cask, apt, uv, …). It shows how something got onto the machine, but not whether this repo declared it or which role owns it.

The existing `tv aliases` channel, the precedent the user remembers, builds its list at runtime from `alias` / `typeset -f`. That works for aliases but not for tools: an install inventory needs data that has been *declared*.

**Outcome:** one structured catalog file becomes the single source of truth for tool metadata. A new `tv inventory` channel reads it and checks each tool's live status on this host, and the Tool index in tool-managers.md is generated from the catalog instead of being written by hand.
````

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Parse Tool index table into JSON rows

```bash
mkdir -p /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-zhouhanru--local-share-chezmoi/948183d8-effa-431b-8fac-7072a591dd51/scratchpad && cd /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-zhouhanru--local-share-chezmoi/948183d8-effa-431b-8fac-7072a591dd51/scratchpad && cat > parse_index.py <<'EOF'
import re, json, sys
src = open('/Users/zhouhanru/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md').read().splitlines()
start = src.index('| Tool | macOS | Linux | Role |')
rows=[]
for line in src[start+2:]:
    if not line.startswith('|'): break
    # split on | not inside backticks
    cells=[];cur='';tick=False
    for ch in line[1:]:
        if ch=='`': tick=not tick
        if ch=='|' and not tick: cells.append(cur.strip());cur=''
        else: cur+=ch
    assert len(cells)==4,(line,cells)
    rows.append(cells)
print(len(rows))
json.dump(rows,open('rows.json','w'),ensure_ascii=False,indent=0)
EOF
python3 parse_index.py
```

```text
      # further down. It is the one tool this repo installs from GitHub
      # releases on macOS too, because upstream disables `herdr update` on
      # Homebrew installs and that removes the only pane-preserving upgrade
      # path. docs/tools/herdr.md has the reasoning.
      - btop
      - htop
      - duckdb
      - rclone
      # skopeo — registry client that does the network itself instead of asking
      # the Docker daemon to. That matters under the GFW: `docker pull` runs in
      # the daemon, which ignores the shell's proxy env, so an image no mirror
      # carries is unreachable until you restart the daemon with a proxy.
      # `skopeo copy docker://REF docker-daemon:REF` honours HTTPS_PROXY and
      # writes straight into the daemon — no restart. It is rung 3 of
      # `docker-net pull`; see docs/tools/docker-net.md.
      - skopeo
      # mosh — mobile shell; roaming UDP-based SSH replacement that survives
      # IP changes / sleep / high latency. mosh-server listens on UDP
      # 60000-61000, which cloud hosts must open inbound.
      - mosh
      - coreutils
      - taplo
      - television
      - pandoc
      - tailspin
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = []
# ///
"""Reader for the repo's tool catalog, used by the `inventory` tv channel.

The catalog (``~/.config/docs/tools/tool-catalog.toml``, source
``dot_config/docs/tools/tool-catalog.toml``) is the SSOT for "what does this
repo install, what is it, which role installs it". This script joins it with
live host state:

  * chezmoi data (the init prompts) → is the tool's gate on for this host?
  * PATH / /Applications probes       → is it actually installed?

Subcommands:
    source                  TSV for tv: id, status, category, role, method, desc, display
    preview ID              human-readable detail (tv preview + Enter)
    cmd ID {install,upgrade,docs,bin}
                            print one derived value (tv actions)
    index-md [--write FILE | --check FILE]
                            render the tool-managers.md Tool index table
                            (`just gen-tool-index`)

Status icons: ✅ installed · ❌ expected but missing · ⚪ gated off by an init
prompt · – not for this OS · · nothing to probe (plugins, fonts, libraries).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import platform
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

HOME = Path.home()
DEFAULT_CATALOG = HOME / ".config/docs/tools/tool-catalog.toml"
BEGIN = "<!-- BEGIN generated: tool-catalog (just gen-tool-index) -->"
END = "<!-- END generated: tool-catalog -->"
INDEX_HEADER = ["| Tool | macOS | Linux | Role |", "|---|---|---|---|"]

ICON = {"ok": "✅", "missing": "❌", "gated": "⚪", "na": "–", "unknown": "·"}
LABEL = {
    "ok": "installed",
    "missing": "expected but missing",
    "gated": "not enabled on this host",
    "na": "not for this OS",
    "unknown": "nothing to probe",
}
# Tools whose `--version` is slow, launches a GUI, or isn't a thing.
NO_VERSION_CATEGORIES = {"GUI Apps", "Fonts & Input", "System Libraries"}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Loading
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def load_catalog(path: Path | None = None) -> dict:
    path = path or Path(os.environ.get("TOOL_CATALOG", DEFAULT_CATALOG))
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        return tomllib.load(fh)


def load_chezmoi_data() -> dict:
    """Prompt answers. Read chezmoi.toml directly (fast); fall back to the CLI."""
    cfg = HOME / ".config/chezmoi/chezmoi.toml"
    try:
        with open(cfg, "rb") as fh:
            data = tomllib.load(fh).get("data", {})
        if data:
            return data
    except (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError):
        pass
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            ["chezmoi", "data", "--format", "json"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10, check=True,
        ).stdout
        return json.loads(out)
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return {}


def host_os() -> str:
    return "darwin" if platform.system() == "Darwin" else "linux"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Derivations (pure — unit-tested)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def is_na(cell: str) -> bool:
    c = cell.strip().lower()
    return c.startswith("n/a") or c.startswith("—") or c in {"", "-"}


def method_for(tool: dict, os_name: str) -> str:
    if os_name == "darwin":
        return tool.get("mac", "")
    linux = tool.get("linux", "")
    return tool.get("mac", "") if linux.strip().lower().startswith("same") else linux


def role_for(tool: dict, os_name: str) -> str:
    if os_name == "linux" and tool.get("role_linux"):
        return tool["role_linux"]
    return tool["role"]


def gate_for(tool: dict, roles: dict, os_name: str) -> str:
    if os_name == "linux" and "gate_linux" in tool:
        return tool["gate_linux"]
    if "gate" in tool:
        return tool["gate"]
    return roles.get(role_for(tool, os_name), {}).get("gate", "")


def eval_gate(expr: str, data: dict, defaults: dict) -> bool:
    if not expr:
        return True
    for term in expr.split("&"):
        term = term.strip()
        neg = term.startswith("!")
        term = term.lstrip("!")
        if "=" in term:
            key, want = term.split("=", 1)
            val = data.get(key, defaults.get(key))
            ok = str(val) == want
        else:
            val = data.get(term, defaults.get(term, False))
            ok = bool(val)
        if ok == neg:
            return False
    return True


def applies_to_os(tool: dict, roles: dict, os_name: str) -> bool:
    role = roles.get(role_for(tool, os_name), {})
    if "os" in role and os_name not in role["os"]:
        return False
    return not is_na(method_for(tool, os_name))


def bins_of(tool: dict) -> list[str]:
    return tool["bins"] if "bins" in tool else [tool["id"]]


def install_cmd(tool: dict, roles: dict, os_name: str) -> str:
    role_name = role_for(tool, os_name)
    role = roles.get(role_name, {})
    if "install" in role:
        return role["install"]
    tag = tool.get("tag") or role.get("tag") or role_name
    return f"just ansible-tags {tag}"


_UPGRADE_RULES = [
    ("ya pkg", "just upgrade-yazi-plugins"),
    ("uv tool", "just upgrade-uv"),
    ("dotnet", "just upgrade-dotnet"),
    ("gem", "just upgrade-gem"),
    ("npm", "just upgrade-npm"),
    ("cargo", "just upgrade-cargo"),
    ("go install", "just upgrade-go"),
    ("mise", "just upgrade-mise"),
    ("flatpak", "just upgrade-flatpak"),
    ("brew", "just upgrade-brew"),
]


def upgrade_cmd(tool: dict, os_name: str) -> str:
    if tool.get("upgrade"):
        return tool["upgrade"]
    role = role_for(tool, os_name)
    if role == "personal_tools":
        return "just upgrade-personal"
    if role == "coding_agents":
        return "just upgrade-agents"
    method = method_for(tool, os_name).lower()
    for needle, cmd in _UPGRADE_RULES:
        if needle in method:
            return cmd
    if any(w in method for w in ("apt", "yum", "dnf", "snap", "system")):
        return "system package manager (apt/dnf upgrade) — not covered by just upgrade-*"
    return "re-run the installer — see docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Probing
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def find_app(app: str) -> Path | None:
    for base in (Path("/Applications"), HOME / "Applications", Path("/System/Applications")):
        p = base / f"{app}.app"
        if p.exists():
            return p
    return None


def probe(tool: dict, os_name: str) -> list[str]:
    """Paths found for this tool (empty = not found)."""
    found: list[str] = []
    if os_name == "darwin" and tool.get("app"):
        p = find_app(tool["app"])
        if p:
            found.append(str(p))
    for b in bins_of(tool):
        w = shutil.which(b)
        if w:
            found.append(w)
    return found


def status_of(tool: dict, cat: dict, data: dict, os_name: str) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    roles = cat.get("roles", {})
    if not applies_to_os(tool, roles, os_name):
        return "na", []
    found = probe(tool, os_name)
    if found:
        return "ok", found
    if not eval_gate(gate_for(tool, roles, os_name), data, cat.get("gate_defaults", {})):
        return "gated", []
    has_probe = bool(bins_of(tool)) or (os_name == "darwin" and tool.get("app"))
    return ("missing" if has_probe else "unknown"), []


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Commands
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def find_tool(cat: dict, tool_id: str) -> dict:
    for t in cat["tool"]:
        if t["id"] == tool_id:
            return t
    sys.exit(f"tool-catalog: unknown id {tool_id!r}")


def cmd_source(cat: dict) -> None:
    os_name = host_os()
    data = load_chezmoi_data()
    order = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(cat.get("categories", []))}
    tools = sorted(cat["tool"], key=lambda t: (order.get(t["category"], 99), t["id"]))
    width = max(len(t["id"]) for t in tools)
    out = sys.stdout
    for t in tools:
        st, _ = status_of(t, cat, data, os_name)
        icon = ICON[st]
        # ✅ ❌ ⚪ are double-width; pad the narrow ones so columns line up.
        icon_cell = icon if st in ("ok", "missing", "gated") else icon + " "
        role = role_for(t, os_name)
        method = " ".join(method_for(t, os_name).replace("`", "").split())
        display = f"{icon_cell} {t['id']:<{width}}  [{t['category']}]  {t['desc']}  ({role})"
        row = [t["id"], icon, t["category"], role, method, t["desc"], display]
        out.write("\t".join(c.replace("\t", " ") for c in row) + "\n")


def _version(tool: dict, found: list[str]) -> str:
    if tool["category"] in NO_VERSION_CATEGORIES:
        return ""
    exe = next((f for f in found if not f.endswith(".app")), None)
    if not exe:
        return ""
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(
            [exe, "--version"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=2,
            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        )
        line = (r.stdout or r.stderr).strip().splitlines()
        return line[0][:100] if line else ""
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return ""


def cmd_preview(cat: dict, tool_id: str) -> None:
    t = find_tool(cat, tool_id)
    os_name = host_os()
    roles = cat.get("roles", {})
    data = load_chezmoi_data()
    st, found = status_of(t, cat, data, os_name)
    gate = gate_for(t, roles, os_name)
    B, D, R = "\033[1m", "\033[2m", "\033[0m"

    def row(k: str, v: str) -> None:
        if v:
            print(f"{D}{k:<10}{R}{v}")

    print(f"{B}{t['id']}{R}  —  {t['desc']}")
    print(f"{D}{'─' * 60}{R}")
    reason = LABEL[st]
    if st == "gated":
        reason += f"  (prompt gate `{gate}` is off — enable via `chezmoi init` / chezmoi.toml)"
    elif st == "ok" and gate and not eval_gate(gate, data, cat.get("gate_defaults", {})):
        reason += f"  (gate `{gate}` is off — installed by something else?)"
    row("status", f"{ICON[st]} {reason}")
    for f in found:
        row("path", f)
    row("version", _version(t, found) if found else "")
    row("category", t["category"])
    row("role", role_for(t, os_name) + (f"   gate: {gate}" if gate else ""))
    row("macOS", t.get("mac", ""))
    row("Linux", t.get("linux", ""))
    row("install", install_cmd(t, roles, os_name))
    row("upgrade", upgrade_cmd(t, os_name))
    row("docs", t.get("docs", ""))
    bins = bins_of(t)
    if bins:
        row("bins", "  ".join(f"{b} {'✓' if shutil.which(b) else '✗'}" for b in bins))
    if t.get("app"):
        row("app", f"{t['app']}.app")
    if t.get("role_md"):
        print(f"\n{D}notes{R}\n{t['role_md']}")


def cmd_value(cat: dict, tool_id: str, what: str) -> None:
    t = find_tool(cat, tool_id)
    os_name = host_os()
    roles = cat.get("roles", {})
    if what == "install":
        print(install_cmd(t, roles, os_name))
    elif what == "upgrade":
        print(upgrade_cmd(t, os_name))
    elif what == "docs":
        print(t.get("docs", ""))
    elif what == "bin":
        bins = bins_of(t)
        print(next((b for b in bins if shutil.which(b)), bins[0] if bins else t["id"]))
    else:
        sys.exit(f"tool-catalog: unknown field {what!r}")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tool index generation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def index_rows(cat: dict) -> list[str]:
    def key(t: dict) -> str:
        return (t.get("label") or t["id"]).replace("*", "").lower()

    lines = list(INDEX_HEADER)
    for t in sorted(cat["tool"], key=key):
        label = t.get("label") or f"**{t['id']}**"
        role = t.get("role_md") or (
            f"{t['role']} / {t['role_linux']}" if t.get("role_linux") else t["role"]
        )
        lines.append(f"| {label} | {t.get('mac', '')} | {t.get('linux', '')} | {role} |")
    return lines


def render_region(cat: dict) -> str:
    return "\n".join([BEGIN, *index_rows(cat), END])


def splice(text: str, region: str) -> str:
    try:
        start = text.index(BEGIN)
        end = text.index(END, start) + len(END)
    except ValueError:
        sys.exit(f"tool-catalog: marker region not found ({BEGIN!r} … {END!r})")
    return text[:start] + region + text[end:]


def cmd_index(cat: dict, argv: list[str]) -> int:
    region = render_region(cat)
    if not argv:
        print(region)
        return 0
    mode, target = argv[0], Path(argv[1])
    text = target.read_text()
    new = splice(text, region)
    if mode == "--check":
        if new != text:
            print(f"{target}: Tool index is stale — run `just gen-tool-index`", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        return 0
    if mode == "--write":
        if new != text:
            target.write_text(new)
            print(f"updated {target}")
        return 0
    sys.exit(f"tool-catalog: unknown flag {mode!r}")


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    catalog_path = None
    if len(argv) >= 2 and argv[0] == "--catalog":
        catalog_path, argv = Path(argv[1]), argv[2:]
    if not argv:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    cat = load_catalog(catalog_path)
    sub, rest = argv[0], argv[1:]
    if sub == "source":
        cmd_source(cat)
    elif sub == "preview" and rest:
        cmd_preview(cat, rest[0])
    elif sub == "cmd" and len(rest) == 2:
        cmd_value(cat, rest[0], rest[1])
    elif sub == "index-md":
        return cmd_index(cat, rest)
    else:
        print(__doc__)
        return 2
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
    except BrokenPipeError:
        sys.exit(0)
```

```toml
# inventory channel — every tool THIS REPO installs, what it is, who installs it,
# and whether it is actually present on this host.
#
# Thin channel: all logic lives in ~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py, which
# reads the SSOT ~/.config/docs/tools/tool-catalog.toml (source:
# dot_config/docs/tools/tool-catalog.toml) and joins it with chezmoi data (the
# init prompts) + PATH / /Applications probes.
#
# Status column (fuzzy-type the icon to filter):
#   ✅ installed · ❌ expected but missing (gate on, not found — a broken install)
#   ⚪ gated off by an init prompt on this host · – not for this OS
#   · nothing to probe (yazi plugins, gh extensions, fonts)
# Also type a category ("Networking"), a role ("python_uv_tools") or a word
# from the description.
#
# vs neighbours: `tv tools` = curated quick-launcher (cli-tools.md);
# `tv appsrc` = live OS scan of how *anything* got installed (repo or not).
#
# Usage:
#   tv inventory
#
# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace — tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows Ctrl+;
# T/M match `tv appsrc`):
#   Enter      Full detail (paged)
#   Alt+T      tldr — quick usage
#   Alt+M      man page
#   Alt+D      Open the tool's doc page (glow → bat → less)
#   Alt+I      Copy the install command (e.g. `just ansible-tags devtools`)
#   Alt+U      Copy the upgrade command (e.g. `just upgrade-uv`)
#   Alt+W      `appsrc which <bin>` — live cross-check of how it was installed
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel

[metadata]
name = "inventory"
description = "Tools this repo installs — category, installing role/recipe, installed / missing / gated-off on this host"
requirements = ["uv"]

[source]
command = "~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py source"
# id<TAB>status<TAB>category<TAB>role<TAB>method<TAB>desc<TAB>display
display = "{split:\\t:6}"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[preview]
command = "~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py preview '{split:\\t:0}'"

[ui]
input_header = "Repo tool inventory"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:detail"
alt-t = "actions:tldr"
alt-m = "actions:man"
alt-d = "actions:docs"
alt-i = "actions:copy-install"
alt-u = "actions:copy-upgrade"
alt-w = "actions:appsrc"

[actions.detail]
description = "Full detail (paged)"
command = "~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py preview '{split:\\t:0}' | less -R"
mode = "execute"

[actions.tldr]
description = "tldr page (multi-language fallback)"
command = "b=$(~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py cmd '{split:\\t:0}' bin); tldr -L zh_TW -L zh -L en \"$b\" 2>/dev/null || \"$b\" --help 2>&1 | head -60; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.man]
description = "man page"
command = "man \"$(~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py cmd '{split:\\t:0}' bin)\""
mode = "execute"

[actions.docs]
description = "Open the repo doc page for this tool"
command = """
d=$(~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py cmd '{split:\\t:0}' docs)
if [ -z "$d" ]; then echo 'No doc page recorded for this tool (add `docs = ...` in tool-catalog.toml).'; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _; exit 0; fi
f="$(chezmoi source-path 2>/dev/null)/$d"
if command -v glow >/dev/null 2>&1; then glow -p "$f"; elif command -v bat >/dev/null 2>&1; then bat --paging=always "$f"; else less "$f"; fi
"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy-install]
description = "Copy the install command"
command = "c=$(~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py cmd '{split:\\t:0}' install); if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' \"$c\" | x copy; elif command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' \"$c\" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' \"$c\" | wl-copy; else printf '%s' \"$c\" | xclip -selection clipboard; fi"
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy-upgrade]
description = "Copy the upgrade command"
command = "c=$(~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py cmd '{split:\\t:0}' upgrade); if command -v x >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' \"$c\" | x copy; elif command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' \"$c\" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' \"$c\" | wl-copy; else printf '%s' \"$c\" | xclip -selection clipboard; fi"
mode = "fork"

[actions.appsrc]
description = "appsrc which — how was it really installed?"
command = "appsrc which \"$(~/.config/television/tool-catalog.py cmd '{split:\\t:0}' bin)\"; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

```
